title: NYC TLC Driver License Exam
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file); null for HTML pages

questions.question: How many questions are on the TLC Driver License Exam?
questions.explanation: The TLC Driver License Exam has 80 multiple-choice questions.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: The exam is made up of 80 multiple-choice questions.

questions.question: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass the TLC Driver License Exam?
questions.explanation: The pass mark is 70%, which is 56 of the 80 questions.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: must answer 56 out of 80 questions correctly to pass

questions.question: How much time do you have to complete the TLC Driver License Exam?
questions.explanation: PSI's bulletin says you have 2 hours for the 80 questions.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: The exam is 80 questions and you will have 2 hours to complete it.

questions.question: Who gives the TLC Driver License Exam?
options: PSI Testing Services, on a computer
questions.explanation: TLC contracts with PSI to give the exam on a computer at PSI test centers.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: The exam is given on a computer by PSI Testing Services.

questions.question: How much does each attempt at the TLC Driver License Exam cost?
options: Nothing; it is included in the $252 fee
questions.explanation: Each attempt costs $49, paid to PSI. Exam fees are not refundable or transferable.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: The TLC Driver License exam is $49 for each exam, which you will pay to PSI.

questions.question: What must you finish before PSI will let you register for the TLC Driver License Exam?
options: The New TLC Driver License Course (3-day)
questions.explanation: PSI will not register you unless you have completed the 3-day (24-hour) course at a TLC-approved school.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: You must complete the 3-day course at a TLC approved school before taking the TLC Driver License Exam.

questions.question: Which courses does the TLC Driver License Exam test?
options: The DMV road test and written test
The renewal course and PED course
The 3-day course and the WAV course
questions.explanation: The exam covers what is taught in the 3-day driver license course and the Passenger Assistance and WAV training.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: Exam covers the topics covered in the 3-day course and WAV course.

questions.question: You fail the TLC Driver License Exam. How soon can you take it again?
options: Only after you reapply to TLC
questions.explanation: You must wait 24 hours before retesting, and you pay the $49 fee again.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: You must wait 24 hours if you want to take the TLC Driver License Exam again.

questions.question: How many times may you take the TLC Driver License Exam?
options: Once; a fail means a new application
As many times as needed until your application expires
questions.explanation: There is no attempt limit, but you must pass before your 90-day application expires.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: You may take the TLC Driver License Exam as many times as you like until your TLC application expires.

questions.question: How early should you arrive at the PSI test center?
questions.explanation: Arrive 15 minutes early to check in. If you arrive after your start time you cannot test and you lose the $49.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: You must arrive at the PSI test center 15 minutes before your scheduled appointment time

questions.question: Up to when can you cancel or reschedule your exam appointment at no extra cost?
options: Up until 2 days before the appointment
Up until 1 hour before the appointment
Only 2 weeks or more before the exam
Up until the morning of the exam
questions.explanation: You can cancel or reschedule free up to 2 days before. Later than that, you lose the $49.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: You may cancel or reschedule your exam appointment up until 2 days before the appointment at no extra cost.

questions.question: Which reference does PSI give you in the exam room?
options: A copy of TLC Rules Chapter 80
A GPS tablet with a map app
questions.explanation: PSI provides a Geographia NYC Five Borough Street Atlas, a Manhattan Address Key, blank paper and a pencil or pen. Calculators are not allowed.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: Geographia NYC Five Borough Street Atlas

questions.question: Which ID must you show to get into the TLC exam room?
questions.explanation: Bring your state-issued DMV driver license. It must match your registered name, show your photo and not be expired.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: Bring your state-issued DMV driver license to the test center to be let into the exam room.

questions.question: Which of these is a language you can choose for the TLC Driver License Exam?
questions.explanation: PSI offers the exam in English, Bengali, Urdu, Simplified Chinese, Russian, Arabic and Spanish.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: English, Bengali, Urdu, Simple Chinese, Russian, Arabic or Spanish

questions.question: When do you find out whether you passed the TLC Driver License Exam?
options: On the computer screen right after you submit
By mail about two weeks later
questions.explanation: The pass or fail result appears on screen when you submit. PSI also emails your results within 48 hours.

source.title: TLC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (PDF)
source.quote: You will find out if you passed the TLC Driver License Exam on the computer screen after you submit your exam.

questions.question: An applicant is disqualified from the TLC Driver License Exam. For how long can TLC deny a new application?
options: One year from the exam date
Six months from the exam date
Three years from the exam date
questions.explanation: Disqualification from the exam is grounds for a three-year ban, counted from the date of that exam.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: The three-year ban will be counted from the date of the examination the applicant was disqualified from.

questions.question: How long is the New TLC Driver License Course (the "24-hour course")?
questions.explanation: The new driver course is 24 hours of classroom instruction: 8 hours a day over 3 days.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: This course is 3 days (8 hours per day) of classroom instruction

questions.question: Within how many days of filing must a new applicant finish all TLC license requirements?
questions.explanation: TLC denies a new application if all requirements are not completed within 90 days of filing.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: has not completed all of the requirements of an Application within 90 days of the date the Application is filed.

questions.question: How long is the Passenger Assistance and Wheelchair Accessible Vehicle (WAV) training?
options: Six hours in a classroom only
At least 3 hours of class plus 1 hour hands-on
questions.explanation: The WAV course is at least 3 hours of classroom time with a 1-hour hands-on assessment.

source.title: TLC: Licensing Education
source.quote: The course is at least three (3) hours of classroom time with one (1) hour of hands -on assessment.

questions.question: How old can your Defensive Driving Course certificate be when you apply for a new TLC license?
questions.explanation: The DDC certificate must have been issued no more than three years before the application date.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: issued no more than three years prior to the application date

questions.question: What is the minimum age to apply for a TLC Driver License?
questions.explanation: TLC Driver License applicants must be at least 19. (Paratransit and commuter van applicants can be 18.)

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: An Applicant for a TLC Driver License must be at least 19 years of age.

questions.question: Which New York State DMV license classes qualify you to apply for a TLC Driver License?
options: Class A, B, C or E
questions.explanation: You need a chauffeur's license: commercial class A, B or C, or for-hire class E.

source.title: TLC: Get a TLC Drivers License
source.quote: Commercial Classes (A, B, C) or For-hire Class (E)

questions.question: To qualify, an applicant may have no more than how many DMV points within a 15-month period?
questions.explanation: TLC requires no more than 5 DMV points within 15 months, counted back from the most recent conviction.

source.title: TLC: Get a TLC Drivers License
source.quote: No more than 5 points on your DMV license within a 15 month period

questions.question: A new applicant tests positive on the TLC drug test. What happens?
options: The license is denied, and the decision is final
They pay a $200 fine and continue
They may retest the next day
questions.explanation: A positive drug test means the application is denied and the decision is final.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: If an Applicant tests positive for drugs or controlled substances, the Commission will deny the Applicant's license and such decision is final.

questions.question: While your application is pending, your mailing address changes. What must you do?
options: Inform TLC of the material change
Withdraw and file a new application
questions.explanation: Applicants must tell TLC about any material change, such as a new address, a new conviction or a change in chauffeur's license status.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: The Applicant must inform the Chairperson of any material change in the information submitted as part of the Application while the Application is pending.

questions.question: How much is the TLC application fee for a new three-year TLC Driver License?
questions.explanation: The license fee is $84 a year, so $252 for a three-year license. It is non-refundable.

source.title: TLC: Get a TLC Drivers License
source.quote: $252 – For a three (3) Year License

questions.question: How do you apply for a new TLC Driver License?
options: In person at the Long Island City office
questions.explanation: TLC's application guide says you must apply online, at nyc.gov/lars, and cannot apply in person.

source.title: TLC Driver License Application Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must apply online. You cannot apply in-person.

questions.question: How long is a new TLC Driver License valid?
options: Five years from the date it was issued
One year from the date it was issued
Three years from the date it was issued
questions.explanation: A new license expires three years from its issue date. Renewals run three years from the old expiration date.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A License issued to a new Applicant will expire three years from the date the License was issued.

questions.question: At least how long before your license expires must you file a renewal application?
questions.explanation: File at least 30 days early. Later applications may not be reviewed before the license expires.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A renewing Applicant must file a completed application at least 30 days before the expiration date of the License.

questions.question: Your TLC license expired last month. Can you still renew it?
options: Yes, within 180 days, with a $25 late fee
No, you must take the 3-day course again
Yes, at any time, with no fee
questions.explanation: You can file a late renewal up to 180 days after expiration with a $25 late fee. The license stays invalid until TLC approves it.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: up to 180 days after the expiration date as a "late application," if the Applicant pays a late fee of $25.

questions.question: A driver keeps working after the TLC license expires while the renewal is still being processed. What is this?
options: Allowed if the renewal fee is paid
questions.explanation: Driving for hire after the license expires and before the renewal is issued is Unlicensed Activity.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: after his or her License expires and before a renewal License is issued is engaged in Unlicensed Activity.

questions.question: Your TLC Driver License is lost or stolen. How quickly must you notify TLC in writing?
options: Within 72 hours, not counting weekends and holidays
questions.explanation: Notify TLC in writing within 72 hours (weekends and holidays not counted).

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: within 72 hours (not counting weekends and holidays).

questions.question: You move. Within how many days must you report the new mailing address to TLC?
questions.explanation: Drivers must report a change of mailing or email address within ten days.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver must report any change of Mailing Address and E-mail Address to the Commission in a manner prescribed by the Commission within ten days.

questions.question: Which history can lead TLC to deny an application for one year?
options: One parking ticket in the past year
More than three collisions within a single year
questions.explanation: More than three collisions in a single year can trigger a one-year ban, counted from the last collision.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: More than three Collisions within a single year.

questions.question: Which City agency holds hearings and issues rulings on TLC driver violations?
options: OATH (Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings)
questions.explanation: OATH handles summonses and issues rulings on driver violations.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH) is the city agency responsible for court proceedings, summonses, and issuing rulings for driver violations

questions.question: You are found guilty of a TLC violation and do not appeal. When is the fine due?
questions.explanation: Fines are due within 30 days of a guilty finding. Unpaid fines lead to license suspension.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Fines are due within 30 days of the day the Respondent is found guilty of the violation

questions.question: What is the fine for letting another person use your TLC Driver License or Technology System login?
questions.explanation: Letting someone use your license or login, or using someone else's, is fined $10,000 with revocation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Fine: $10,000 and revocation

questions.question: During your shift, may someone else drive your vehicle or sit in the driver's seat?
options: Yes, for up to one hour
Yes, if they have a DMV license
questions.explanation: During the work shift no one else may operate the vehicle or occupy the driver's seat, except in an emergency.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not allow another person to operate the Vehicle or occupy the Driver's seat, except in the event of an emergency.

questions.question: May a driver tip a Port Authority dispatcher or baggage handler at the airport?
options: No, any gift to them is prohibited
questions.explanation: Licensees must not give any gift, gratuity or thing of value to Port Authority or terminal staff such as dispatchers, security or baggage handlers.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not offer or give any gift, gratuity, or thing of value to anyone at the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey

questions.question: A public servant asks you for a gift. Who must you report this to right away?
options: TLC and the NYC Department of Investigation
questions.explanation: Any request or demand for a gift by a public servant must be reported at once to TLC and DOI.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must immediately report to the Commission and the NYC Department of Investigation any request or demand for a gift

questions.question: What is the penalty for sexual contact with any person while working as a TLC licensee?
questions.explanation: Sexual contact while performing licensee duties is fined $2,000 with mandatory revocation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Fine: $2,000 and mandatory revocation.

questions.question: Which act toward a service animal is a TLC violation?
options: Distracting or trying to distract it
Opening the rear door for it
Asking if it is a service animal
Letting it ride on the floor
questions.explanation: Licensees must not distract, harm or use force against a service animal.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not distract or attempt to distract any Service Animal.

questions.question: When may a TLC vehicle stop and wait for passengers right in front of a fire hydrant?
options: When the hazard lights are on
When the driver stays seated, ready to drive
questions.explanation: Unless expressly forbidden, a vehicle may stop in front of a hydrant to wait for passengers if the driver stays seated and ready.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: permitted to stop and wait for Passengers in the space immediately in front of a fire hydrant on a street, provided the Driver remains seated

questions.question: How many TLC points are given for speeding 11 to 20 mph over the posted limit?
questions.explanation: Speeding 11–20 mph over is 4 points (1–10 over is 3; 21–30 over is 5).

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: SPEEDING 11 to 20 miles above posted speed limit 4

questions.question: How long after drinking any alcohol must a driver wait before driving or occupying the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers must not drive or occupy their vehicle for at least six hours after consuming any alcohol or drugs.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver must not drive or occupy his or her Vehicle for at least six hours after consuming any intoxicating liquor

questions.question: Which TLC drivers are exempt from annual drug testing?
options: Black car and luxury limousine drivers
NYC police officers and paratransit drivers
Drivers with no violations in three years
Drivers over age 65 with a doctor's note
questions.explanation: Every driver must pass a drug test each year except NYC police officers and paratransit drivers.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: All Drivers except (1) Drivers who are City of New York Police Officers or (2) Paratransit drivers, must be tested annually

questions.question: What is the most total time a driver may transport passengers for hire in any 24-hour period?
questions.explanation: The daily limit is 10 hours of passenger time in any 24-hour period.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not transport any Passenger(s) for hire for more than 10 hours in total in any 24-hour period.

questions.question: What resets a driver's 10-hour daily count?
options: Carrying no passengers for at least 8 consecutive hours
Logging off the Technology System for 30 minutes
Switching to a different TLC-licensed vehicle
The clock passing midnight at the end of each day
questions.explanation: If a driver carries no passengers for at least eight consecutive hours, the 10-hour count resets.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: If a Driver transports no Passengers for hire for at least eight consecutive hours, the 10-hour count resets

questions.question: What is the weekly limit on hours transporting passengers for hire?
questions.explanation: Drivers may not carry passengers for more than 60 hours in a Monday-to-Sunday week.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: more than 60 hours in total in any seven-day period that begins on Monday and ends on Sunday.

questions.question: When may a TLC driver use a cell phone?
options: While moving below 10 mph in slow traffic
While stopped at a red light in traffic
Any time, as long as it is hands-free
Only while the vehicle is lawfully standing or parked
questions.explanation: Drivers must not use an electronic communication device while operating the vehicle; use is allowed only when lawfully stopped or parked.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver can Use an Electronic Communication Device only while the Vehicle is lawfully standing or parked.

questions.question: How many TLC points does a first phone-use violation carry?
questions.explanation: A first or second offense in 15 months is 3 points; a third is 4 points.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Points: 3 for the first offense and for the second offense in any 15-month period;

questions.question: What is the speed limit in New York City unless a sign says otherwise?
questions.explanation: TLC's study guide teaches the 25 mph citywide default limit.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The speed limit in NYC is 25 miles per hour (mph), unless otherwise posted.

questions.question: Is turning right on a red light allowed in New York City?
options: No, unless a sign permits it
questions.explanation: Turning on red is illegal in NYC unless posted otherwise.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Turning at a red light is illegal in NYC, unless otherwise posted.

questions.question: How much space should you leave between your vehicle and a cyclist?
options: At least 3 feet in all directions
questions.explanation: Leave at least 3 feet; cyclists need room for potholes and opening doors.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Leave at least 3 feet between you and the cyclist in all directions.

questions.question: Under the NYS seat belt law, when could the driver be ticketed for an unbuckled passenger?
options: The passenger is under 16 and has no parent or guardian
The trip is shorter than one mile
The passenger is any adult in the back
questions.explanation: Since November 2020 all passengers must buckle up. The driver can be ticketed if an unaccompanied passenger under 16 is not buckled.

source.title: TLC: Seat Belt Law
source.quote: If a driver is transporting a passenger under the age of 16, and they are not accompanied by a parent or guardian

questions.question: What is the penalty for having a weapon in your TLC vehicle without the Chairperson's written permission?
questions.explanation: Possessing a weapon in the vehicle while operating it is punished by revocation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Fine: Revocation

questions.question: May a driver smoke in the vehicle between trips when no passenger is inside?
options: No, smoking in the vehicle is not allowed
questions.explanation: The rule is simply that a driver must not smoke in a vehicle.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver must not smoke in a Vehicle.

questions.question: When may a driver lock the rear doors while on duty?
options: Only with the passenger's consent or request, or as the rules allow
Any time after dark, for the driver's safety
Whenever the meter is running and the car moves
Whenever a passenger has put luggage in the trunk
questions.explanation: Rear doors may not be locked except with passenger consent or request, or for reasons in the rules (such as going off duty).

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not lock either of the rear doors except with the consent or at the request of a Passenger

questions.question: Four adults are in a four-passenger taxi. When must you accept one more passenger?
options: When it is a child under 7 held on an adult's lap in the rear
Never; four is the limit with no exceptions
When the fifth adult agrees to sit in the front seat
When it is a child under 12 sitting in the front
questions.explanation: An extra passenger must be accepted if under age seven and held on the lap of an adult in the rear.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: an additional Passenger must be accepted if the Passenger is under the age of seven (7) and is held on the lap

questions.question: A passenger's wheelchair takes up the rear seat. Where may the passenger sit?
options: Nowhere; the trip must be refused
questions.explanation: If luggage or a mobility aid occupies the rear seats, the passenger must be allowed in the front seat.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: a Passenger must be permitted to occupy the front passenger seat.

questions.question: May a taxi driver sell or recommend products to passengers?
options: Yes, if the item costs under $20
No, not without prior written TLC approval
questions.explanation: Drivers must not sell, advertise or recommend services or goods without written approval. FHV and SHL drivers may promote their base's services.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver must not sell, advertise or recommend any service or merchandise to any Passenger without prior written Commission approval.

questions.question: How long may a TLC vehicle's engine idle?
options: As long as a passenger is aboard
questions.explanation: Under the NYC Air Pollution Control Code, engines must not idle longer than three minutes.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not cause or permit the engine of the Vehicle to idle for longer than three minutes.

questions.question: Which equipment must a driver keep checking is in good working order?
options: Brakes, tires, lights, signals and passenger seatbelts
Only the radio and air conditioning
questions.explanation: Drivers must continually inspect brakes, tires, lights, signals, and passenger seat and shoulder belts.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: including brakes, tires, lights, signals and passenger seatbelts and shoulder belts, is in good working order.

questions.question: A passenger gives no route preference. Which route must you take?
questions.explanation: Follow reasonable, lawful routing requests; otherwise take the shortest reasonable route.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Unless a Passenger makes a specific request, a Driver must proceed to the Passenger's destination by the shortest reasonable route.

questions.question: Mid-trip, a passenger asks to change the destination. What must you do?
options: End the trip and restart the meter
Comply, unless it is impossible or unsafe
Refuse; the original destination is binding
questions.explanation: Passengers may change or end the ride during the trip; drivers must comply unless impossible or unsafe.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Drivers must comply with these requests unless it is impossible or unsafe.

questions.question: A passenger asks you to put their suitcase in the trunk. What must you do?
options: Load it only if it is light
Load it, and unload it at the end
questions.explanation: On request, the driver must load and unload luggage, wheelchairs, crutches or other property and close the trunk securely.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Upon the request of a Passenger, the Driver must load or unload a Passenger's luggage, wheelchair, crutches or other property

questions.question: Which phone number must be on a taxi receipt?
questions.explanation: Taxi and SHL receipts must include the 311 complaint number along with the fare details and hack license number.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: the "311" Commission Complaint telephone number.

questions.question: A passenger asks for your name and TLC license number. What must you do?
questions.explanation: Drivers must comply with reasonable requests for their name, TLC license number and the vehicle's license number.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must provide comply with all reasonable Passenger requests to provide his or her name, TLC Driver License number

questions.question: What happens to a driver who charges or tries to charge $10 or more above the approved fare?
options: A written warning for a first offense
The TLC Driver License is revoked
A $50 fine and a refund to the passenger
questions.explanation: Overcharging by $10 or more brings mandatory revocation, and the driver may have to repay the passenger.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: the Taxi and Limousine Tribunal at OATH or the Chairperson will revoke the Driver License

questions.question: What is the fine for a first overcharge or refusal violation if the driver pleads guilty before a hearing?
questions.explanation: First violation: $350 if you plead guilty before a hearing, $500 if found guilty after one.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: First violation: $350 if plead guilty before a hearing; $500 if found guilty following a hearing.

questions.question: A passenger travels with a service animal and a wheelchair. What extra may you charge?
questions.explanation: No additional charge may be imposed for a person with a disability, a service animal, or a wheelchair or other mobility aid.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not impose or attempt to impose any additional charge for transporting a person with a disability, a service animal

questions.question: A taxi passenger refuses to pay the fare. What should you do?
options: Lock the doors and call your garage to come
Let them go and report it at your license renewal
Keep the passenger's bag until the fare is paid
Record the fare and go directly to the nearest police precinct
questions.explanation: Turn the meter to vacant, record the fare, go straight to the nearest precinct and follow the police's instructions.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: proceed directly to the nearest police precinct, present the facts to the police and follow their instructions

questions.question: Your taxi's card system is down. When may you still pick up a passenger?
options: If you tell them before starting the meter that cards won't work
Only if you take the card number by hand
Never; you must go off duty
questions.explanation: You may carry the passenger only if, before engaging the meter, you tell them they will not be able to pay by card.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: unless prior to engaging the Taximeter, the Driver advises the Passenger that he/she will not be able to use a credit or debit card

questions.question: A passenger wants to go to Connecticut in your taxi. How is the fare set?
options: A flat dollar amount agreed before the trip
Double the meter outside the City
questions.explanation: For destinations outside the City other than Westchester, Nassau and Newark Airport, negotiate a flat dollar amount first. "Double the meter" is not a flat rate.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A "flat" rate means a dollar amount; "double the meter" is NOT a flat rate.

questions.question: How is a taxi fare to Westchester or Nassau County calculated?
options: Double the meter for the whole trip
The standard meter for the whole trip
Meter to the City limit, then double the meter
questions.explanation: The meter runs the whole way; the portion beyond the City limit is charged at double (Rate #04).

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: The metered fare is double the amount from the City limit to your destination.

questions.question: What is the surcharge for a taxi trip to Newark Airport?
questions.explanation: Newark trips are the standard meter plus a $20 Newark surcharge, plus tolls both ways.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: Plus $20.00 Newark Surcharge.

questions.question: On a taxi trip to Newark Airport, who pays the driver's return tolls?
questions.explanation: Passengers pay tolls to and from Newark, including the driver's return tolls.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: passengers are charged for the drivers' return tolls

questions.question: What is the flat fare between Manhattan and JFK Airport (before surcharges, tips and tolls)?
questions.explanation: Manhattan–JFK trips in either direction are a $70 flat fare plus surcharges, tip and tolls.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: Trips between Manhattan and John F. Kennedy Airport (JFK) in either direction: $70

questions.question: What rush-hour surcharge applies to the Manhattan–JFK flat fare on weekdays from 4 to 8 p.m.?
questions.explanation: The JFK flat fare carries a $5.00 rush-hour surcharge (4–8 p.m. weekdays, not legal holidays).

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: $5.00 rush hour surcharge (4pm to 8pm weekdays, excluding legal holidays).

questions.question: How is a taxi trip to or from LaGuardia Airport charged?
options: A flat rate negotiated before the trip
A $70 flat fare in either direction
Double the meter from the City limit
questions.explanation: LGA trips are the standard metered fare plus a $5 surcharge and other applicable surcharges.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: Trips to and from LaGuardia Airport (LGA) are charged the standard metered fare, plus a $5.00 surcharge

questions.question: What is the initial charge on the standard taxi meter?
questions.explanation: The standard metered fare starts at $3.00, plus 70 cents per 1/5 mile or per 60 seconds slow or stopped.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: $3.00 initial charge. Plus 70 cents per 1/5 mile

questions.question: When does the $2.50 rush-hour surcharge apply to metered taxi trips?
options: All day Friday and Saturday evenings
4 to 8 p.m. every day, including holidays
7 to 10 a.m. on weekdays, except holidays
4 to 8 p.m. on weekdays, except holidays
questions.explanation: The rush-hour surcharge is $2.50 from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays, excluding holidays.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: Plus $2.50 rush hour surcharge from 4pm to 8pm on weekdays, excluding holidays.

questions.question: A yellow taxi trip passes through Manhattan below 96th Street. What New York State Congestion Surcharge applies?
questions.explanation: The NYS Congestion Surcharge is $2.50 for yellow taxis, $2.75 for green taxis and 75 cents for shared rides.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: Plus New York State Congestion Surcharge of $2.50 (Yellow Taxi) or $2.75 (Green Taxi) or 75 cents (any shared ride)

questions.question: What is the MTA Congestion Pricing toll for yellow and green taxis in the zone at and below 60th Street?
questions.explanation: Taxis pay a 75-cent congestion pricing toll for trips in Manhattan at or below 60th Street, with some highway exclusions.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: Plus MTA Congestion Pricing toll of 75 cents for Yellow and Green Taxi for the area of Manhattan south of and including 60th Street

questions.question: Which of these is free for taxi passengers?
questions.explanation: There is no charge for extra passengers, luggage or paying by credit card.

source.title: TLC: Taxi Fare
source.quote: There is no charge for extra passengers, luggage or bags, or paying by credit card.

questions.question: A taxi trip starts in NYC and ends in which of these places requires the MTA Tax?
questions.explanation: The MTA Tax applies to trips from NYC ending in NYC or Dutchess, Nassau, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Suffolk or Westchester counties.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: (5) Putnam County. (6) Rockland County. (7) Suffolk County. (8) Westchester County.

questions.question: What must you do right after a trip to JFK, LaGuardia or Newark Airport?
options: Check the interior and trunk for left property
questions.explanation: After an airport trip, inspect the interior and trunk (if used) to make sure passengers took their property.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: the Driver must inspect the interior of the Vehicle and the trunk compartment, if used, to ensure that Passengers have collected their property.

questions.question: You find a wallet in your taxi and cannot return it to the passenger. Where must it go?
options: A police precinct, as NYPD directs
questions.explanation: Return it to the passenger if possible; otherwise take it without delay to a police precinct as NYPD directs.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: otherwise, it must be taken without delay to a police precinct as directed by the NYPD.

questions.question: Where else, besides a police precinct, may an FHV or SHL driver take unreturned lost property?
options: The TLC Long Island City office
questions.explanation: In an FHV or SHL, lost property can go to a police precinct or to the vehicle's base.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: taken without delay to a police precinct as directed by the NYPD or to the Vehicle's Base.

questions.question: How close to an authorized Taxi Stand may a taxi driver cruise for passengers?
questions.explanation: Taxi drivers must not solicit or cruise within 100 feet of an authorized Taxi Stand.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Within 100 feet of any authorized Taxi Stand

questions.question: You are logged off and heading to your garage. When may you pick up a passenger?
options: Never; once logged off you cannot carry anyone
Only if they are waiting at an authorized taxi stand
If they agree in advance to a negotiated flat fare
If their destination is directly on your route and you recorded it
questions.explanation: Logged off, you may take a passenger only if you are returning home or to the garage, have recorded it, and their destination is directly on the route.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: The Passenger's destination is directly on the route to the Driver's home or garage.

questions.question: May a taxi driver pick up an additional passenger during a trip?
options: Yes, if going the same way
Only at the current passenger's request
questions.explanation: Drivers must not pick up more passengers during a trip unless the passenger asks, and must not suggest it.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not pick up additional Passengers during a trip except at the Passenger's request.

questions.question: Where may a green Street Hail Livery NOT accept street hails?
options: Anywhere in the Bronx and on Staten Island
Anywhere in Queens and Brooklyn, except the airports
Manhattan south of E. 96th and W. 110th Streets, and the airports
Manhattan north of 125th Street and the Bronx
questions.explanation: That area is the Hail Exclusionary Zone. SHLs may accept hails everywhere else in the City (the Hail Zone).

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 51: Definitions (PDF)
source.quote: Hail Exclusionary Zone is the area in which Street Hail Liveries are NOT permitted to accept a passenger by hail.

questions.question: How may a For-Hire Vehicle driver (black car, livery, app) pick up passengers?
options: Only by prearrangement through a licensed base
questions.explanation: FHV drivers must not solicit or pick up passengers except by prearrangement through a licensed base.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not solicit or pick up Passengers other than by prearrangement through a licensed Base

questions.question: What is the fine for an FHV driver's first street pickup in Manhattan below E. 96th/W. 110th or at an NYC airport?
questions.explanation: In the Hail Exclusionary Zone the enhanced penalty is $500, then $750, then revocation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Fine: First Violation: $500 Second Violation in 24 months: $750 Third Violation in 120 months: Revocation

questions.question: May an FHV driver pick up passengers waiting at a Taxi Stand?
options: Yes, if the stand is empty of taxis
questions.explanation: FHV drivers must not pick up at any Taxi Stand. First violation is $350; the third in 36 months is revocation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A For-Hire Driver must not pick up Passengers at any Taxi Stand.

questions.question: May a green SHL take a spot at a Taxi Stand in Midtown Manhattan?
options: No, not in the Hail Exclusionary Zone
Yes, if no taxis are waiting
questions.explanation: SHL drivers may use Taxi Stands in the Hail Zone but not in the Hail Exclusionary Zone.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver of a Street Hail Livery does NOT have the right to take a position at a Taxi Stand in the Hail Exclusionary Zone.

questions.question: Which destinations must a taxi driver take a passenger to?
options: Anywhere in Manhattan, plus JFK and LaGuardia only
Anywhere in NYC, Westchester, Nassau or Newark Airport
Anywhere in New York State or New Jersey
Anywhere within 25 miles of the pickup point
questions.explanation: Mandatory transport covers any destination in NYC, Westchester or Nassau counties, or Newark Airport.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: to any destination within the City of New York, the counties of Westchester or Nassau, or Newark Airport.

questions.question: A taxi driver asks a person's destination before they get in, then agrees to take them. Is that a violation?
options: Yes, asking in advance is a violation anyway
No, because the driver took the trip
No, if the trip was short
questions.explanation: Trying to learn the destination before the passenger is seated is a violation even if the driver then takes the trip.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Attempting to learn the destination in advance is a violation of this paragraph, regardless if the Driver ultimately agrees to transport the Passenger.

questions.question: A passenger has a pet cat loose in their arms. May you refuse the trip?
options: Yes, an animal not in a suitable container is a valid reason
No, every animal must be accepted, in a carrier or not
Only if you show a doctor's note for an allergy
Only after 8 p.m., when overnight rules apply
questions.explanation: You may refuse a passenger with an animal not properly secured in a container, but this never applies to service animals.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: The Passenger is accompanied by an animal that is not properly secured in a suitable container.

questions.question: A passenger keeps smoking during the trip. What must you do before making them leave?
options: Ask them to stop at least twice
Nothing; you may stop at once
questions.explanation: If they refuse to stop, you may discharge them in a safe place, but only after asking at least twice.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: The Driver must ask the Passenger at least twice to stop smoking before requiring him or her to leave the Vehicle.

questions.question: You may refuse items you reasonably believe will damage the vehicle. Which of these may you NOT refuse?
questions.explanation: The damage exception never covers wheelchairs, crutches, service animals or other mobility aids.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: This does NOT include wheelchairs, crutches, a service animal or other mobility aid used by a Passenger with a Disability.

questions.question: May a driver require a passenger with a disability to bring an attendant?
questions.explanation: Requiring an attendant is a refusal violation with mandatory penalties. Attendants also ride at no extra charge.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver must not require a person with a disability to be accompanied by an attendant.

questions.question: You accept a hail through an E-Hail app, then decide not to take the passenger. What is this?
options: Allowed if you cancel in the app
Allowed if the pickup is far
A refusal subject to mandatory penalties
questions.explanation: Refusing a passenger after accepting their E-Hail is a refusal with mandatory penalties.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A Driver must not refuse to transport a Passenger after accepting a Hail from that Passenger by means of an E-Hail Application.

questions.question: A passenger wants to make three stops before the final destination. May you refuse?
options: Yes, more than one stop may be refused
No; multiple stops are allowed on one meter
questions.explanation: Drivers may not refuse passengers with more than one stop; the meter runs continuously for the whole trip.

source.title: TLC: Passenger Frequently Asked Questions
source.quote: Drivers are not permitted to refuse passengers with more than one stop.

questions.question: According to the Green Taxi Passenger Bill of Rights, must a Boro Taxi passenger share a ride?
options: No, not unless they want to
questions.explanation: Green taxi passengers have the right not to share a ride unless they want to.

source.title: TLC: Green Taxi Passenger Bill of Rights
source.quote: Not share a ride, unless you want to;

questions.question: Who may drive an accessible (wheelchair accessible) taxi?
options: Only drivers with 5 years of TLC driving experience
An Approved Driver who completed WAV training or has a paratransit license
Only the owner of the medallion for that vehicle
Any TLC driver with a valid TLC Driver License
questions.explanation: Accessible vehicles may be driven only by Approved Drivers.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 53: Accessible Taxicabs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: An Accessible Vehicle can only be driven by an Approved Driver

questions.question: While operating an accessible vehicle, may you decline a trip from the Accessible Taxi Dispatcher?
options: Yes, if it is over 1 mile away
questions.explanation: Approved Drivers must accept dispatches; not accepting is a refusal with mandatory penalties.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 53: Accessible Taxicabs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: While operating an Accessible Vehicle, an Approved Driver must accept a dispatch from the Accessible Taxi Dispatcher.

questions.question: You have accepted an accessible dispatch. A person hails you on the way. What do you do?
options: Take them if they pay cash
Take them and tell the dispatcher
Take them if going the same way
Do not pick them up before the dispatched passenger
questions.explanation: After accepting a dispatch you must not accept any other passenger, including an e-hail, before picking up the dispatched passenger.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 53: Accessible Taxicabs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must not accept any other Passenger before picking up the Passenger with a mobility impairment.

questions.question: On an accessible dispatch, when may you turn on the taximeter?
options: After the passenger is seated and secured
When you arrive at the pickup
When you start loading the ramp
questions.explanation: Do not start the meter until the passenger is seated and secured.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 53: Accessible Taxicabs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: MUST NOT turn on the Taximeter when dispatched by the Accessible Taxi Dispatcher until the Passenger is seated and secured in the vehicle.

questions.question: After arriving for an accessible dispatch (on-demand), how long must you wait for the passenger?
questions.explanation: Wait at least ten minutes after your reported arrival (or after the scheduled time for advance reservations).

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 53: Accessible Taxicabs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: must wait for the passenger with a disability to appear curbside at the pick up point for at least ten minutes

questions.question: Who pays the Dispatch Fee on an Accessible Dispatch trip?
options: The passenger, added to the fare
questions.explanation: Passengers pay the metered fare. The Dispatch Fee is paid to the driver and is never charged to the passenger.

source.title: TLC: Accessible and E-hail Trips: What Drivers Need to Know (PDF)
source.quote: Remember, the passenger never pays the Dispatch Fee.

questions.question: A passenger with a disability needs help getting out. When must the meter go to non-recording?
options: Before you start helping them exit
When they are on the sidewalk
It stays on until the door closes
questions.explanation: Put the meter in non-recording before assisting, and leave it there until they have paid and safely exited.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: the Driver must place the Taximeter in a non-recording position before assisting such Passenger

questions.question: How many securements should you always offer a passenger who uses a wheelchair?
questions.explanation: Offer all six: four floor straps plus the lap belt and shoulder belt.

source.title: TLC: Wheelchair Securement Tips decal (PDF)
source.quote: Always offer all six (6) securements to passengers.

questions.question: Where do you attach securement straps on a manual wheelchair?
questions.explanation: On manual chairs, secure straps on the frame; on motorized chairs, use the loops at the base.

source.title: TLC: Wheelchair Securement Tips decal (PDF)
source.quote: For manual chairs, secure straps on the frame of the chair. Do not secure straps on the wheels.

questions.question: A passenger in a wheelchair declines some of the securements. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Offer all securements, but if a passenger declines some or all, respect their choice.

source.title: TLC: Accessible and E-hail Trips: What Drivers Need to Know (PDF)
source.quote: If a passenger declines some or all of the securements, please respect their choice.

questions.question: A WAV passenger has a service animal and three companions. Whom must you carry?
options: The animal and all companions who can legally be seated
The passenger, the animal and one companion
The companions, but not the animal
Only the passenger and the wheelchair
questions.explanation: Approved Drivers must carry the service animal(s) and as many companions as can legally be seated.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 53: Accessible Taxicabs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: for as many companions as can be legally seated in the vehicle.

questions.question: Which item must a taxi or SHL have on board?
options: A five-borough street map or GPS device
A first-aid kit and road flares
A spare taximeter and receipt roll
A fire extinguisher and spare tire
questions.explanation: Required items include the Technology System, displayed TLC license and rate card, and a five-borough map or GPS.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: A New York City five (5) borough indexed street map or geographic position system device.

questions.question: After sunset, which items must be lit so a rear-seat passenger can see them?
options: The radio display and the air vents
Taximeter, TLC Driver License and Rate Card
The trunk light and the license plate light
Only the roof light and the rear dome light
questions.explanation: After sunset the meter face, TLC license and rate card must be illuminated and visible from the rear seat.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: the face of the Taximeter, his or her TLC Driver License, and the Rate Card are illuminated

questions.question: The Technology System stops working during your shift. What must you do?
options: Take cash only for the rest of the day
Fix it before accepting new trips
Keep working and write paper records
questions.explanation: If the Technology System malfunctions, it must be fixed before you accept any new trips.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: the Driver must fix the Technology System before accepting any new trips to transport passengers

questions.question: The taximeter breaks during a trip. What options must you offer the passenger?
options: Agree a reasonable fare to continue, or end and pay the meter so far
Continue free of charge to the destination
Get out right away without paying anything
Continue and pay double the last meter reading
questions.explanation: Tell the passenger immediately and offer to continue at a mutually agreed reasonable fare, or end the trip and pay the meter to that point.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: Continuing the trip after mutually agreeing to a reasonable fare, or

questions.question: When must a taxi's roof light be on?
options: When on duty, available and the meter is not in use
Whenever the engine is running, on or off duty
Only at night, from sunset to sunrise
Whenever a passenger is aboard and paying
questions.explanation: The roof light is lit when you are on duty and available with the meter off, and off when the meter is in use or you are unavailable.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: The Roof Light must be illuminated when the Taximeter is not in use and the Driver is on duty and available

questions.question: Where must an FHV driver's TLC Driver License usually be displayed?
options: In the glove compartment, shown on request
Taped to the inside of the rear window
On the dashboard, facing out the windshield
In a holder on the back of the driver's seat
questions.explanation: FHV drivers display the license in a protective holder on the back of the driver's seat. Black cars and luxury limousines have an exception.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: displayed in a protective holder attached to the back of the driver's seat in the Vehicle.

questions.question: Besides specific penalties, what may TLC impose at its discretion for a rule violation?
options: Jail time of up to 30 days and a $500 fine
Revocation, suspension up to six months and/or a fine up to $1,000
A fine of up to $100, with no suspension
Only a written warning on the driver's record
questions.explanation: Discretionary penalties: revocation, suspension of up to six months, and/or a fine of up to $1,000 per violation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: revocation, License suspension of up to six months, and/or a fine, not to exceed $1,000

questions.question: Under the Persistent Violator Program, what happens at 6 to 9 points within 15 months?
questions.explanation: Six to nine combined TLC and DMV points in 15 months means suspension for up to 30 days.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: accumulated a total of at least six but fewer than ten TLC Points or DMV Points or both combined

questions.question: How many combined points within 15 months lead to revocation under the Persistent Violator Program?
questions.explanation: Ten or more TLC and/or DMV points in 15 months means revocation.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: accumulated a total of 10 or more TLC Points or DMV Points or both combined

questions.question: How many points does a Point Reduction Course remove before suspension or revocation?
questions.explanation: Completing a Point Reduction Course deducts three TLC points (a DMV Defensive Driving Course deducts three DMV points).

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: will deduct three TLC Points from the points accumulated by any Licensee who voluntarily attends and satisfactorily completes a Point Reduction Course

questions.question: A driver's third parking or moving violation in 15 months brings a suspension. How can they avoid it?
options: Wait 15 months for the points to expire
Retake the 3-day New TLC Driver License Course
Pay double the fine within 30 days
Complete the Vision Zero and Accessibility course within 60 days
questions.explanation: The suspension is deferred 60 days and lifted if the driver completes the Vision Zero and Accessibility Remedial course in that time.

source.title: TLC Rules Chapter 80: Drivers of Taxicabs, FHVs and SHLs (PDF)
source.quote: if the Driver completes a Vision Zero and Accessibility Remedial education course within the 60-day period, the Driver will not be suspended.

questions.question: Brooklyn is also which county?
questions.explanation: Brooklyn is Kings County; Manhattan is New York County; Staten Island is Richmond County.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Brooklyn is a borough in New York City. The borough is also Kings County in New York State.

questions.question: In Manhattan, which way do avenue numbers increase?
questions.explanation: Avenues run north–south and their numbers increase as you go west (First Avenue is east, Eighth is west).

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Avenues run North/South and the numbering increases as you drive West.

questions.question: In general, which way do even-numbered Manhattan streets run?
questions.explanation: In general, even-numbered streets run east and odd-numbered streets run west.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: streets in Manhattan run East if even numbered, and West if odd numbered

questions.question: In Midtown Manhattan, which avenue divides the East Side from the West Side?
questions.explanation: Fifth Avenue is the dividing line in Midtown; it runs one way downtown. Downtown, Broadway is the divider.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: In Midtown Manhattan, Fifth Avenue is the dividing line between the East and West side.

questions.question: Which street is the boundary between Uptown and Midtown Manhattan?
questions.explanation: 59th Street divides Uptown and Midtown; 14th Street divides Midtown and Downtown.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: 59th street is the boundary between Uptown and Midtown

questions.question: What does Park Avenue become below 14th Street?
questions.explanation: Park Avenue becomes Fourth Avenue below 14th Street.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Park Avenue becomes Fourth Avenue below 14th Street

questions.question: What does Eighth Avenue become at Columbus Circle?
questions.explanation: Eighth Avenue becomes Central Park West at Columbus Circle, then Frederick Douglass Boulevard at 110th Street.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: 8th Avenue becomes Central Park West at Columbus Circle

questions.question: At what street does the FDR Drive become the Harlem River Drive?
questions.explanation: The FDR Drive's name changes to Harlem River Drive at 120th Street.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The name changes to Harlem River Drive at 120th Street.

questions.question: Where is Grand Central Terminal?
questions.explanation: Grand Central is at Park Avenue and East 42nd Street. Penn Station is at Seventh Avenue and West 32nd Street.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Grand Central Terminal - Park Avenue at East 42nd Street, Manhattan

questions.question: JFK Airport is at the end of which highway?
questions.explanation: JFK sits at the end of the Van Wyck Expressway in Queens. LaGuardia is near the Grand Central Parkway.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Kennedy (JFK) Airport - At the end of the Van Wyck Expressway, Queens

questions.question: The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge connects which two boroughs?
questions.explanation: The Verrazzano-Narrows is a toll bridge over New York Harbor between Brooklyn and Staten Island.

source.title: TLC Driver Education Course & Exam Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Verrazano-Narrows Bridge Toll New York Harbor Brooklyn - Staten Island

questions.question: The Goethals Bridge crosses the Arthur Kill between Staten Island and where?
questions.explanation: The Goethals Bridge (toll) links Staten Island and New Jersey, as do the Outerbridge Crossing and the Bayonne Bridge.

source.quote: Goethals Bridge Toll Arthur Kill Staten Island - New Jersey
